title: Build Momentum, Consequence, and Narrative Integrity Into Every Act
use_cases: Use when drafting a screenplay to ensure a coherent structure that sustains pressure from the first act to the final consequence.
Implement when revising a script to strengthen the middle and second act, preventing structural collapse.
Configure when editing to align character arcs with decision-driven development rather than traits.
Apply when analyzing a draft to identify where stakes diffuse or conflict misaligns with narrative progression.
Use when coaching writers to build load‑bearing design rather than following rigid templates.
content:
Most screenplays do not collapse because of bad dialogue or weak description.

They collapse because the structure cannot bear the weight placed on it.

A screenplay that “holds” is not one that follows a formula. It is one that sustains pressure from the first act to the final consequence without loosening its logic, diffusing its stakes, or betraying its premise.

Structure is not a template. It is load-bearing design.

This guide breaks down how professional screenplay structure actually works, why most scripts fall apart, and how to build one that survives both readers and development.
